longForm.heroLead: Moisture testing shouldn't take hours. The Computrac® MAX 4000XL cuts loss-on-drying analysis down to minutes — up to 100x faster than a standard oven reference method, and 25% faster than other rapid LOD instruments on the market. The speed comes from a built-in lid fan that rapidly cools the heating chamber between tests. Less waiting, more samples through the door. Accuracy doesn't get traded away for speed. A 100-microgram resolution balance delivers repeatable, defensible results, run after run. The enclosure is all-steel. The heating element is nickel chromium. Built for the lab bench and the production floor alike. What it measures: moisture and solids content, across food, pharmaceutical, plastics, and chemical applications. What it stores: 250 test programs, 1,000 results, 100 graphs — all on the instrument. What it shows: real-time moisture curves and rate-of-loss data, live, on a large color display.

body.text: Loss-on-drying moisture and solids analyzer. Precise, repeatable results across industrial applications.

Menu-driven interface. User-programmable settings, no steep learning curve.
Optional web server. Download calibration reports, view the screen remotely, pull audit logs, upload or download test programs and results.
Stores 250 programs, 1,000 results, 100 graphs. History stays on the instrument.
Free expert support from Brookfield's moisture analysis specialists.

sections.title: Rapid Cooling and Throughput
sections.tabSummary: Why the lid fan is the whole speed story
body: Why the lid fan is the real story behind the 25% figure.
Loss-on-drying testing has a bottleneck most people don't think about: the chamber has to cool before the next sample goes in. Every minute spent cooling is a minute the instrument isn't testing.
MAX 4000XL's built-in lid fan solves that directly. It cools the heating chamber fast, and Brookfield states the result plainly: 25% faster throughput than other rapid loss-on-drying instruments.
That's not a marginal gain. Across a full shift of testing, 25% is the difference between finishing the queue and carrying samples into tomorrow.

paragraphs: Not all moisture behaves the same way. Some evaporates fast and easily — free moisture. Some is chemically bound to the material and needs a different temperature, a different endpoint, to release.

MAX 4000XL links multiple test stages into one sequence. Temperature, ending criteria, and timing can all change between segments — so a single run captures both free and bound moisture without manual intervention between stages.
User-adjustable ending criteria go further: the test stops when your material says it's done, not when a generic default says so.

faqs.question: What is the Computrac MAX 5000XL used for?
faqs.answer: Moisture, solids, and ash analysis from a single sample, using loss-on-drying and loss-on-ignition methods, across plastics, pharmaceuticals, foods, and biomass materials.

faqs.question: What is the maximum heater temperature?
faqs.answer: Up to 600°C, high enough to run both LOD and LOI tests.

faqs.question: How is this different from a thermogravimetric analyzer?

faqs.answer: 30 minutes or less.

faqs.answer: Cast aluminum, built for heavy-duty use in the lab or on the production floor.

faqs.question: Does it need manual cleaning after high-temperature tests?

faqs.question: Can it measure ash content?
faqs.answer: Yes, via loss-on-ignition testing, made possible by the 600°C heater.

faqs.question: Can moisture, solids, and ash all come from one sample?
faqs.answer: Yes, using multistage testing that adjusts temperature and ending criteria across linked segments.

faqs.question: Can the solution be accessed remotely?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the optional web server feature, remote LCD viewing, calibration report downloads, audit log access, and program transfer between solutions.

faqs.question: How is MAX 5000XL different from MAX 4000XL?
faqs.answer: MAX 5000XL reaches 600°C and adds loss-on-ignition testing for ash content, positioned as a TGA alternative. MAX 4000XL is built for fast moisture-only testing via loss-on-drying.

sections.title: Moisture-Specific Detection, Not Weight Loss
sections.tabSummary: Why RH-sensor technology changes what gets measured
body: Computrac Vapor Pro XL detection method: why RH-sensor technology changes what gets measured.

Loss-on-drying and loss-on-ignition methods measure how much mass a sample loses when heated, then assume the loss is moisture. That assumption breaks down when a sample contains other volatile compounds. The instrument can't tell the difference, and the result reads high.

Vapor Pro XL sidesteps that problem entirely. RH-sensor technology detects moisture specifically, not total mass loss, which means the result reflects actual water content even in samples where other volatiles are present. Sensitivity reaches 10 micrograms of water, low enough to determine moisture content as low as 10ppm, a level weight-loss methods typically can't resolve reliably.
